page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs, corresponding to 32 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system includes 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance is network and EBS optimized with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and specialized execution capabilities. The instance achieves a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU encryption tests. It also demonstrates strong performance in software compilation using Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Database operations on Passmark are rated strong, while memory bandwidth, single-core execution, and Redis SET operations perform within average ranges. LLM text generation for small and medium models also registers strong token throughput.

Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage, this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The qualitative cost profile reflects its positioning as a high-tier, specialized resource where the expense of large-scale RAM is offset by consolidated database and in-memory processing capabilities. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, electronic design automation, and heavy data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 64 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz, paired with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance delivers 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and database operations, alongside average single-core and memory bandwidth results. With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per core, this instance provides qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating massive in-memory databases and data processing workloads onto a single node. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
